notes: T927 (does a run's wall clock survive a host sleep?): FIXED + measured. Defect: nothing in the dispatch path called caffeinate, so the host could idle-sleep mid-measurement and silently inflate the wall figure (tools/runner computes wall as end - start, folding any sleep into the number with no signal in the record). 2026-08-24 slept 24x (765-900s each, all 03:14-08:23 local); any wall figure taken that day is suspect. FIX (tools/runner): hold a `caffeinate -i -w <runner-pid>` assertion for the child's lifetime. -i prevents idle sleep; -w <pid> makes caffeinate wait for the runner to exit, so the assertion auto-releases on EVERY exit path including a SIGKILL of the runner (caffeinate detects the pid gone) — the same discipline the arbiter release needs. caffeinate is a child of the RUNNER (not the guarded child), so the child's process-group reap never touches it and it is never counted in the child's RSS. The run record gains `sleep_prevented` (true|false, stamped at LAUNCH so a SIGKILL of the runner before finalize cannot erase it) and `sleeps_during_run` (N, from `pmset -g log` 'Entering Sleep' entries whose timestamp falls in the run window, stamped at finalize; None = not measured). A run that slept is MARKED, not discarded — the reader decides. On a non-darwin/no-caffeinate host the guard honestly reports sleep_prevented=false with a reason, never a silent true. Operator override: `--no-sleep-guard` or `WEIZIGO_SLEEP_GUARD=0` disables the assertion (explicit flag wins, else env, else default ON). TRADEOFF (per the brief): holding idle-sleep off across an unattended fleet night is a power/thermal decision, not just a correctness one — the env override is the route the dispatcher takes for such nights; correctness runs keep it on (the default). The runner does NOT force it unconditionally at the dispatcher level. REGRESSION (test-first, wired into zig build test via tools/regression-sleep-guard.sh): 4 arms — A null (guard ON, short run, no sleep -> sleep_prevented=true, sleeps_during_run=0, both fields present), B seeded-defect (--no-sleep-guard -> sleep_prevented=false), C seeded-defect (WEIZIGO_SLEEP_GUARD=0 -> sleep_prevented=false), D wall-killed run still carries sleep_prevented on the launch record. RED confirmed pre-implementation (all 4 arms failed: fields absent + unknown flag). GREEN: ALL CONTROLS PASSED. GOBAN SCALING LEDGER (docs/infra/host/goban-scaling.jsonl): tools/goban-scaling-capture.sh now holds a caffeinate -i -w <solve-pid> sidecar for each capture and stamps sleep_prevented + sleeps_during_run + start_epoch on every new row (smoke-tested: a 2x2 capture wrote sleep_prevented=true, sleeps_during_run=0). The 8 existing T924 rows were re-stamped in place (git-tracked, recoverable): sleep_prevented=false (true — no caffeinate was used pre-T927), sleeps_during_run=null with reason 'pre-T927: caffeinate not used' (no start_epoch was recorded, so the window is unknowable). SLEEP-SPAN CHECK on existing rows: all 8 rows carry head=7026044, authored 2026-08-25T04:15:36Z (local 06:15) — so every row post-dates the 24-sleep day (2026-08-24, all sleeps 03:14-08:23 local). The only sleep after the commit in the pmset log is a single 40s idle sleep at 2026-08-25T07:16:27Z (local 09:16). The two 4x4 rows (wall 1231s, 1971s) are the only rows with a window long enough that spanning that 40s sleep is plausible; whether one did is UNKNOWABLE (no start_epoch recorded). VERDICT: no existing row can be CONFIRMED to span a sleep, and none can be cleared either; the 24-sleep day predates all rows so the headline suspect day is not represented in the ledger. The honest statement for every existing row is sleep_prevented=false, sleeps_during_run=null (window unknowable). Acceptance `sh tools/regression-sleep-guard.sh` PASSES.
